usageNotes: Use this to modify an existing cluster-wide custom CPU model definition — for example to add or remove CPU flags, change the reported model, or adjust CPUID visibility settings. The caller must hold the Mapping.Modify privilege on /mapping/cpu/{cputype}; the model must already exist (use the POST endpoint to create it). Pass a digest obtained from the GET response to guard against concurrent edits.

examples.summary: Add spec-ctrl and ssbd mitigations to an existing custom CPU model and set reported-model to Haswell

tips: The 'custom-' prefix in the cputype path segment is optional — Proxmox normalises both 'mycpu' and 'custom-mycpu' to the same model.
Use the 'delete' param (comma-separated config key names) to unset optional fields like 'flags' or 'hv-vendor-id' rather than passing empty strings.
Setting 'hidden: true' hides the KVM hypervisor signature from the guest; useful for software that refuses to run under a detected hypervisor.
Setting 'level: 30' is a documented workaround for Hyper-V boot failures on Windows guests running on recent Intel hosts.
Avoid setting 'phys-bits: host' if live migration across heterogeneous hardware is required — mismatched values will break migration.
This endpoint returns null on success; confirm the change by calling the corresponding GET to read back the updated definition.
